findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple cheeses out of date marked and visibly molded. 
1. Sliced Cheddar(date marked July of 2026)
2. Sliced Provolone (date marked August of 2026)
3. Fresh Mozzarella (best by date April of 2026)
4. Shredded Mozzarella (opened and missing date marking)
5. Shredded Lettuce (opened and missing date marking)
All items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking the coolers daily to discard any out of date food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two knives stored in between the knife storage block and the wall. This crevice is not considered easily cleanable and therefore is not safe for utensil storage. Items were moved during the inspection. Ensure that all cooking utensils are stored in a clean, dry location.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the caulking of the mop sink to be damaged. PIC was made aware and work order has been placed. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained and in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The Certified Food Managers (CFMs) were unable to produce Allergen Awareness Training during today’s inspection. Discussed with CFMs, who stated they will be retaking the course, and emailing verification to the inspector. Ensure Allergen Awareness Training is renewed every 3 years and maintained on file during future inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector tested dish machine (puck). Dish machine was ran several times, starting initially at 135F and going up to 152F. Discussed machine not reaching 160F with PIC. PIC immediately put in a service call for the dish machine. Ensure that only triple sink is used until dish machine can be serviced. Inspector will return 04/14/2025 to re-asses dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.111 Manual Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. If immersion in hot water is used for SANITIZING in a manual operation, the temperature of the water shall be maintained at 77°C (171°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer at the dish machine is registering as zero parts per million of chlorine when tested with an indicator strip. The technician arrived and worked on the machine. The machine is now testing at 50ppm chlorine. The violation is considered corrected on site. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The floor in the employee, women’s restroom near the kitchen is in gross disrepair. The floor is cracked in several places, the tile is broken revealing raw concrete and the floor drain appears to be elevated. Repair the floor by the next routine inspection.  
PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an area around the dish machine and the back splash on the dirty dish side of the dish machine to be sealed with white tape. Seal these areas with silicone or a cleanable, durable material.
Also, the seal behind the tee/coffee machines and the cabinet next to the tea/coffee station is showing signs of disrepair. Clean, seal, repair or replace and seal the cabinet in this area.  
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
